quote: It is a prerequisite that the QP certification/confirmation is carried out in full accordance with EU legislation and EU GMP guidelines
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: Remote QP certification/confirmation is carried out fully in line with EU legislation and EU GMP guidelines.

quote: QP certification / confirmation should take place within the EU/EEA (or Northern Ireland) in all cases. This should be demonstrated by technical means.
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: In all cases the QP performs certification/confirmation from within the EU/EEA (or Northern Ireland), and the location is demonstrated by technical means.

quote: QPs are obliged to maintain their knowledge in relation to the products, manufacturing processes and pharmaceutical quality system.
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: QPs keep their knowledge of the products, manufacturing processes and pharmaceutical quality system up to date.

quote: QPs also need to be satisfied that their ongoing reliance on the relevant pharmaceutical quality system is well founded.
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: QPs satisfy themselves that their continuing reliance on the relevant pharmaceutical quality system is well founded.

quote: The QP must be able to demonstrate to the competent authority knowledge of the product and the manufacturing processes for which they are responsible.
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: The QP can show the competent authority that they know the products and manufacturing processes they are responsible for.

quote: This should include time spent physically on-site as applicable.
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: The QP's demonstrated product and process knowledge includes time physically spent on site, as applicable.

quote: Where remote QP certification / confirmation is employed on a routine basis, it must be described and controlled within the pharmaceutical quality system
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: Where remote QP certification/confirmation is used routinely, it is described and controlled within the pharmaceutical quality system.

quote: relevant detailed site procedures should be in place
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: Where remote QP certification/confirmation is used routinely, detailed site procedures covering it are in place.

quote: In Member States where use of contract QPs (i.e. a person who is not an employee of the manufacturer but conducting QP activities under the manufacturer’s authorisation) is permitted, the technical agreement between the MIA holder and the QP should also mention remote certification / confirmation, and specify the circumstances under which the QP must attend the site.
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: In Member States that permit contract QPs, the technical agreement between the MIA holder and the contract QP covers remote certification/confirmation and states when the QP has to attend the site.

quote: The QP should have access to all information (data and computer system applications) which are necessary according to Annex 16 to make a decision on batch certification / confirmation.
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: The QP has access to all data and computer system applications needed under Annex 16 to decide on batch certification/confirmation.

quote: The MIA holder should provide the required facilities to enable QPs to carry out their functions remotely. This includes the equipment and support required to enable electronic batch certification / confirmation and completion of the batch certification register remotely.
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: The MIA holder provides the facilities, equipment and support QPs need to work remotely, including electronic batch certification/confirmation and remote completion of the batch certification register.

quote: IT systems used for remote batch release should comply with requirements of EU GMP Annex 11.
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: IT systems used for remote batch release meet EU GMP Annex 11 requirements.

quote: All actions carried out by the QP electronically at the remote location should be contemporaneously available for inspection by the competent authorities at the authorised batch release site.
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: Every electronic action the QP takes at the remote location is available at the same time for competent authority inspection at the authorised batch release site.

quote: It is the responsibility of the MIA holder to guarantee that a) only the QP has editing access to the batch certification function
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: The MIA holder guarantees that only the QP has editing access to the batch certification function.

quote: that data being transferred are complete and unchanged
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: The MIA holder guarantees that data transferred for remote certification are complete and unchanged.

quote: an electronic signature, reflecting requirements in annex 11, is in place
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: The MIA holder guarantees that an electronic signature meeting Annex 11 requirements is in place.

quote: QPs must be able to demonstrate that they are fulfilling their wider duties in accordance with Annex 16.
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: QPs can show they are fulfilling their wider duties under Annex 16.

quote: Compliance with the above points should be verified e.g. as part of the self-inspection programme at the authorized batch release site.
ref: Questions and answers on remote batch certification / confirmation by the qualified… Q2
statement: Compliance with these remote certification conditions is verified, for example through the self-inspection programme at the authorised batch release site.

quote: Ongoing compliance with the company's data governance policy/procedures should be reviewed during self-inspection, to ensure that they remain effective.
statement: Self-inspections review ongoing compliance with the company's data governance policy and procedures to confirm they remain effective.

quote: This may also include elements of the Data lifecycle discussed in Q3-Q9.
statement: The data integrity self-inspection may also cover elements of the data lifecycle (Q3-Q9).

quote: The main responsibilities of the independent quality unit(s) should not be delegated.
statement: The main responsibilities of the independent quality unit(s) are not delegated.

quote: These responsibilities should be described in writing
statement: The quality unit responsibilities are written down, and include at least the responsibilities listed in this clause.

quote: Releasing or rejecting all APIs. Releasing or rejecting intermediates for use outside the control of the manufacturing company
statement: The quality unit releases or rejects all APIs, and releases or rejects intermediates that will be used outside the manufacturer's control.

quote: Establishing a system to release or reject raw materials, intermediates, packaging and labelling materials
statement: The quality unit sets up a system for releasing or rejecting raw materials, intermediates, packaging materials and labelling materials.

quote: Reviewing completed batch production and laboratory control records of critical process steps before release of the API for distribution
statement: The quality unit reviews the completed batch production and laboratory control records for critical process steps before an API is released for distribution.

quote: Making sure that critical deviations are investigated and resolved
statement: The quality unit ensures critical deviations are investigated and resolved.

quote: Approving all specifications and master production instructions
statement: The quality unit approves all specifications and master production instructions.

quote: Approving all procedures impacting the quality of intermediates or APIs
statement: The quality unit approves every procedure that affects the quality of intermediates or APIs.

quote: Making sure that internal audits (self-inspections) are performed
statement: The quality unit ensures internal audits (self-inspections) are carried out.

quote: Approving intermediate and API contract manufacturers
statement: The quality unit approves contract manufacturers of intermediates and APIs.

quote: Approving changes that potentially impact intermediate or API quality
statement: The quality unit approves changes that could affect intermediate or API quality.

quote: Reviewing and approving validation protocols and reports
statement: The quality unit reviews and approves validation protocols and validation reports.

quote: Making sure that quality related complaints are investigated and resolved
statement: The quality unit ensures quality-related complaints are investigated and resolved.

quote: Making sure that effective systems are used for maintaining and calibrating critical equipment
statement: The quality unit ensures effective systems are in use for maintenance and calibration of critical equipment.

quote: Making sure that materials are appropriately tested and the results are reported
statement: The quality unit ensures materials are tested appropriately and the results are reported.

quote: Making sure that there is stability data to support retest or expiry dates and storage conditions on APIs and/or intermediates where appropriate
statement: The quality unit ensures, where appropriate, that stability data exist to support the retest or expiry dates and storage conditions of APIs and/or intermediates.

quote: Performing product quality reviews (as defined in Section 2.5)
statement: The quality unit performs product quality reviews as defined in Section 2.5.

quote: In order to verify compliance with the principles of GMP for APIs, regular internal audits should be performed in accordance with an approved schedule.
statement: Regular internal audits are carried out to an approved schedule to verify compliance with GMP principles for APIs.

quote: Audit findings and corrective actions should be documented and brought to the attention of responsible management of the firm.
statement: Audit findings and corrective actions are documented and reported to the firm's responsible management.

quote: Agreed corrective actions should be completed in a timely and effective manner.
statement: Agreed corrective actions are completed in a timely and effective way.

quote: The distributor should conduct and record self-inspections in order to monitor the implementation of and com­ pliance with these guidelines.
statement: The distributor carries out and records self-inspections to monitor implementation of, and compliance with, the GDP guidelines.

quote: Regular self-inspections should be performed in accordance with an approved schedule.
statement: Regular self-inspections are performed according to an approved schedule.

quote: establishment and implementation of an effective pharmaceutical quality system
statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether an effective pharmaceutical quality system has been established and implemented.

quote: sufficient competent and appropriately qualified personnel
statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether there are enough competent, suitably qualified personnel.

quote: defined job descriptions for managerial and supervisory staff responsible for manufacturing and quality activities
statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether managerial and supervisory staff for manufacturing and quality activities have defined job descriptions.

quote: training programmes for all staff involved in manufacturing and quality activities
statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether there are training programmes for all manufacturing and quality staff.

quote: training programmes related to health, hygiene and clothing as identified as necessary to the intended operations
statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether there are health, hygiene and clothing training programmes where needed for the intended operations.

quote: provision and maintenance of premises and equipment appropriate to the intended operations
statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether premises and equipment suitable for the intended operations are provided and maintained.

quote: documentation system(s) covering all processes and specifications for the various manufacturing and quality operations
statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether documentation systems cover all processes and specifications for manufacturing and quality operations.

quote: systems for coding and identifying starting materials, intermediates and excipients to allow full traceability
statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether starting materials, intermediates and excipients are coded and identified so they are fully traceable.

quote: qualification program of suppliers
statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether there is a supplier qualification programme.

quote: system for quality control of the excipient and a responsible person independent from production to release the batches
statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether there is a quality control system for the excipient and a responsible person, independent of production, who releases batches.

quote: retention of records for incoming materials and excipients and retention of samples of excipients for the peri­ ods required by EudraLex Volume 4, Part II
statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether records of incoming materials and excipients, and excipient samples, are retained for the periods required by EudraLex Volume 4, Part II.

quote: systems to ensure that any activity contracted out is subject to a written contract
statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether there are systems ensuring every outsourced activity is covered by a written contract.

quote: maintenance of an effective system whereby complaints are reviewed and excipients may be recalled
statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether an effective system is maintained for reviewing complaints and recalling excipients.

quote: change management and deviation management system
statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether there is a change management and deviation management system.

quote: environmental control and storage conditions
statement: Taking account of the excipient's source, supply chain and use, the manufacturing authorisation holder considers, as a minimum, whether environmental control and storage conditions are in place.

quote: Self inspections should be conducted in order to monitor the implementation and compliance with Good Manufacturing Practice principles and to propose necessary corrective measures.
statement: Self-inspections are carried out to monitor implementation of and compliance with GMP principles and to propose any corrective measures needed.

quote: Personnel matters, premises, equipment, documentation, production, quality control, distribution of the medicinal products, arrangements for dealing with complaints and recalls, and self inspection, should be examined at intervals following a pre-arranged programme in order to verify their conformity with the principles of Quality Assurance.
statement: Personnel, premises, equipment, documentation, production, quality control, distribution, complaint and recall arrangements, and self-inspection itself are examined at intervals under a pre-arranged programme to verify conformity with Quality Assurance principles.

quote: Self inspections should be conducted in an independent and detailed way by designated competent person(s) from the company.
statement: Self-inspections are carried out independently and in detail by designated competent company staff.

quote: Independent audits by external experts may also be useful.
statement: Independent audits by external experts may also be used.

quote: All self inspections should be recorded.
statement: Every self-inspection is recorded.

quote: Reports should contain all the observations made during the inspections and, where applicable, proposals for corrective measures.
statement: Self-inspection reports include all observations and, where applicable, proposed corrective measures.

quote: Statements on the actions subsequently taken should also be recorded.
statement: The actions taken after the self-inspection are recorded.

quote: In order to ensure the consistent application of the principles of good manufacturing practice, manufacturers of medicinal products for human use and inspectors should consider the guidelines referred to in the second paragraph of Article 47 of Directive 2001/83/EC.
statement: Manufacturers of human medicinal products take into account the GMP guidelines referred to in Article 47, second paragraph, of Directive 2001/83/EC to apply GMP principles consistently.

quote: However, for advanced therapy medicinal products, the guideline referred in Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 1394/2007 (1) should be applied.
statement: For advanced therapy medicinal products, the guideline referred to in Article 5 of Regulation (EC) No 1394/2007 is applied.

quote: The manufacturer shall be required to conduct repeated self-inspections as part of the pharmaceutical quality system in order to monitor the implementation and respect of good manufacturing practice and to propose any necessary corrective measures and/or preventive actions.
statement: The manufacturer carries out repeated self-inspections within the pharmaceutical quality system to monitor GMP implementation and compliance and to propose any corrective and/or preventive actions needed.

quote: Records shall be maintained of such self-inspections and any corrective actions subsequently taken.
statement: Records are kept of self-inspections and of any corrective actions taken afterwards.

quote: The manufacturer shall conduct regular internal audits
statement: The manufacturer carries out regular internal audits.

quote: follow-up on the findings
statement: The manufacturer follows up on internal audit findings.

quote: Product realisation is achieved by designing, planning, implementing, maintaining and continuously improving a system that allows the consistent delivery of products with appropriate quality attributes
statement: The quality system is designed, planned, implemented, maintained and continuously improved so that products with the right quality attributes are delivered consistently.

quote: Product and process knowledge is managed throughout all lifecycle stages
statement: Product and process knowledge is managed across every lifecycle stage.

quote: Medicinal products are designed and developed in a way that takes account of the requirements of Good Manufacturing Practice
statement: Product design and development take GMP requirements into account.

quote: Production and control operations are clearly specified and Good Manufacturing Practice adopted
statement: Production and control operations are clearly defined and GMP is adopted.

quote: Managerial responsibilities are clearly specified
statement: Management responsibilities are clearly defined.

quote: Arrangements are made for the manufacture, supply and use of the correct starting and packaging materials, the selection and monitoring of suppliers and for verifying that each delivery is from the approved supply chain
statement: Arrangements exist for making, supplying and using the correct starting and packaging materials, for selecting and monitoring suppliers, and for checking each delivery comes from the approved supply chain.

quote: Processes are in place to assure the management of outsourced activities
statement: Processes are in place to manage outsourced activities.

quote: A state of control is established and maintained by developing and using effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality
statement: A state of control is set up and kept through effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality.

quote: The results of product and processes monitoring are taken into account in batch release, in the investigation of deviations, and, with a view to taking preventive action to avoid potential deviations occurring in the future
statement: Product and process monitoring results are used in batch release, in deviation investigations and for preventive action against future deviations.

quote: All necessary controls on intermediate products, and any other in-process controls and validations are carried out
statement: All necessary controls on intermediate products, other in-process controls and validations are performed.

quote: Continual improvement is facilitated through the implementation of quality improvements appropriate to the current level of process and product knowledge
statement: Continual improvement is supported by quality improvements suited to current process and product knowledge.

quote: Arrangements are in place for the prospective evaluation of planned changes and their approval prior to implementation taking into account regulatory notification and approval where required
statement: Planned changes are evaluated in advance and approved before implementation, taking regulatory notification and approval into account where required.

quote: After implementation of any change, an evaluation is undertaken to confirm the quality objectives were achieved and that there was no unintended deleterious impact on product quality
statement: After any change is implemented, it is evaluated to confirm the quality objectives were met and product quality was not harmed unintentionally.

quote: An appropriate level of root cause analysis should be applied during the investigation of deviations, suspected product defects and other problems.
statement: Investigations of deviations, suspected product defects and other problems use an appropriate level of root cause analysis.

quote: In cases where the true root cause(s) of the issue cannot be determined, consideration should be given to identifying the most likely root cause(s) and to addressing those.
statement: Where the true root cause cannot be found, the most likely root cause(s) are considered, identified and addressed.

quote: Where human error is suspected or identified as the cause, this should be justified having taken care to ensure that process, procedural or system- based errors or problems have not been overlooked, if present.
statement: Where human error is suspected or identified as the cause, this is justified after checking that process, procedural or system-based errors have not been overlooked.

quote: Appropriate corrective actions and/or preventative actions (CAPAs) should be identified and taken in response to investigations.
statement: Suitable corrective and/or preventive actions (CAPAs) are identified and implemented following investigations.

quote: The effectiveness of such actions should be monitored and assessed, in line with Quality Risk Management principles.
statement: CAPA effectiveness is monitored and assessed in line with quality risk management principles.

quote: Medicinal products are not sold or supplied before a Qualified Person has certified that each production batch has been produced and controlled in accordance with the requirements of the Marketing Authorisation and any other regulations relevant to the production, control and release of medicinal products
statement: No medicinal product is sold or supplied until a Qualified Person has certified that each batch was produced and controlled in line with the Marketing Authorisation and other applicable production, control and release regulations.

quote: Satisfactory arrangements exist to ensure, as far as possible, that the medicinal products are stored, distributed and subsequently handled so that quality is maintained throughout their shelf life
statement: Arrangements are in place so that, as far as possible, storage, distribution and later handling maintain product quality throughout shelf life.

quote: There is a process for self-inspection and/or quality audit, which regularly appraises the effectiveness and applicability of the Pharmaceutical Quality System.
statement: A self-inspection and/or quality audit process regularly appraises the effectiveness and applicability of the pharmaceutical quality system.

quote: The manufacturer and, where different, marketing authorisation holder should evaluate the results of the review and an assessment made as to whether corrective and preventive action or any revalidation should be undertaken, under the Pharmaceutical Quality System.
statement: The manufacturer, and the marketing authorisation holder where different, evaluate the product quality review results and assess whether corrective and preventive action or revalidation is needed under the pharmaceutical quality system.

quote: There should be management procedures for the ongoing management and review of these actions
statement: Management procedures exist for the ongoing management and review of these actions.

quote: the effectiveness of these procedures verified during self-inspection
statement: The effectiveness of these management procedures is verified during self-inspection.

quote: Quality reviews may be grouped by product type, e.g. solid dosage forms, liquid dosage forms, sterile products, etc. where scientifically justified.
statement: Where scientifically justified, quality reviews may be grouped by product type, such as solid, liquid or sterile dosage forms.

quote: Where the marketing authorisation holder is not the manufacturer, there should be a technical agreement in place between the various parties that defines their respective responsibilities in producing the product quality review.
statement: Where the marketing authorisation holder is not the manufacturer, a technical agreement defines each party's responsibilities for producing the product quality review.

quote: If the report in question was from a routine audit to verify that the firm's quality system is operating as intended, then it would be acceptable if the firm elected to discard the report once all corrections have been verified.
statement: If a report comes from a routine audit verifying that the quality system works as intended, the firm may discard it once all corrections have been verified.

quote: However, any documentation of corrective action as a result of such an audit would have to be retained (see §§ 211.180 and 211.188).
statement: Documentation of corrective actions resulting from an internal audit is retained (21 CFR 211.180 and 211.188).

quote: if a routine internal audit finds a problem with a mixing step and the outcome is a change in mixing time, all affected procedures, including the master production record, are to reflect the necessary changes
statement: If an internal audit leads to a process change (for example a new mixing time), all affected procedures, including the master production record, are updated to reflect it.

quote: Any investigation into the impact this problem had on related batches is to be retained and also made available for inspection by FDA (see § 211.192).
statement: Any investigation of the problem's impact on related batches is retained and made available for FDA inspection (21 CFR 211.192).

quote: Such records are subject to FDA inspection and must be retained for at least the time specified in the CGMP regulations (see § 211.180).
statement: Reports of investigations or evaluations for complaints, vendor qualification, periodic record and data review, and failure investigations are open to FDA inspection and kept for at least the period set in the CGMP regulations (21 CFR 211.180).

quote: The section of a quality agreement that addresses each party’s quality unit activities should define in detail how the parties will work together to ensure that products are manufactured in compliance with CGMP.
statement: The quality unit section of the quality agreement sets out in detail how the parties will work together so products are made in CGMP compliance.

quote: In particular, this section of the quality agreement should be clear with respect to product release.
statement: The quality unit section of the quality agreement is clear about product release.

quote: Contract facilities are responsible for approving or rejecting the product or results of their manufacturing operations (e.g., test results, finished dosage forms, or in-process materials).
statement: The contract facility approves or rejects the products or results of its own manufacturing operations, such as test results, finished dosage forms or in-process materials.

quote: owners are responsible for approving or rejecting drugs manufactured by the contract facility, 23 including for final release.
statement: The owner approves or rejects drugs made by the contract facility, including final release.

quote: In all cases, the owner must not introduce or deliver into interstate commerce, or cause to be introduced or delivered into interstate commerce, any drugs that are adulterated or misbranded.
statement: The owner never introduces, delivers, or causes the introduction or delivery of, adulterated or misbranded drugs into interstate commerce.

quote: Within its quality unit activities, a quality agreement should describe how and when the owner and contract facility will communicate with each other, both verbally and in writing. This includes identifying appropriate contact personnel within the owner’s and contract facility’s organization.
statement: The quality agreement describes how and when owner and contract facility communicate, verbally and in writing, and names the contact people in each organisation.

quote: Quality agreements should also cover audits, inspections, and communication of findings.
statement: The quality agreement covers audits, inspections and communication of findings.

quote: The agreement should allow owners to evaluate and audit contract facilities to ensure CGMP compliance for specific operations. This provision should cover both routine quality audits and for-cause audits.
statement: The quality agreement lets the owner evaluate and audit the contract facility for CGMP compliance of specific operations, covering both routine and for-cause audits.

quote: The agreement should also set owner and contract facility expectations regarding FDA inspections (pre-approval, routine surveillance, and for-cause) with consideration for the nature of the products to be manufactured and/or services to be provided.
statement: The quality agreement sets the owner's and contract facility's expectations for FDA pre-approval, routine surveillance and for-cause inspections, considering the products or services involved.

quote: It should include the parties’ agreed-upon provisions for communicating inspection observations and findings, as well as relevant FDA actions and correspondence.
statement: The quality agreement includes the agreed arrangements for communicating inspection observations and findings and relevant FDA actions and correspondence.

quote: Because contract facilities often provide services to multiple owners, the quality agreement should address when, how, and what information the contractor will report to owners about objectionable conditions observed during inspections and audits of the contract facility.
statement: The quality agreement states when, how and what the contractor will report to the owner about objectionable conditions found during inspections and audits of the contract facility.

quote: Quality systems call for continually monitoring trends and improving systems.
statement: Trends are monitored continually and systems are improved.

quote: Quality systems procedures involve collecting data from monitoring, measurement, complaint handling, or other activities, and tracking this data over time, as appropriate.
statement: Quality system procedures collect data from monitoring, measurement, complaint handling and other activities and track it over time, as appropriate.

quote: the CGMP regulations (§ 211.180(e)) require product review on at least an annual basis
statement: Product review is carried out at least annually as required by 21 CFR 211.180(e).

quote: a quality systems approach calls for trending on a more frequent basis as determined by risk
statement: Data are trended more often than annually, at a frequency set by risk.

quote: A quality systems approach calls for audits to be conducted at planned intervals to evaluate effective implementation and maintenance of the quality system and to determine if processes and products meet established parameters and specifications.
statement: Audits are carried out at planned intervals to evaluate whether the quality system is effectively implemented and maintained and whether processes and products meet established parameters and specifications.

quote: audit procedures should be developed and documented to ensure that the planned audit schedule takes into account the relative risks of the various quality system activities, the results of previous audits and corrective actions, and the need to audit the complete system.
statement: Documented audit procedures ensure the audit schedule accounts for the relative risk of quality system activities, previous audit results and corrective actions, and the need to cover the whole system.

quote: Procedures should describe how auditors are trained in objective evidence gathering, their responsibilities, and auditing procedures.
statement: Procedures describe how auditors are trained in gathering objective evidence, their responsibilities and audit procedures.

quote: Procedures should also define auditing activities such as the scope and methodology of the audit, selection of auditors, and audit conduct (audit plans, opening meetings, interviews, closing meeting and reports).
statement: Procedures define audit activities, including scope and methodology, auditor selection and audit conduct (plans, opening meetings, interviews, closing meeting and reports).

quote: It is critical to maintain records of audit findings and assign responsibility for follow-up to prevent problems from recurring
statement: Records of audit findings are kept and responsibility for follow-up is assigned to prevent recurrence.

quote: The quality systems model calls for managers who are responsible for the areas audited to take timely action to resolve audit findings and ensure that follow-up actions are completed, verified, and recorded.
statement: Managers of audited areas act promptly to resolve audit findings and ensure follow-up actions are completed, verified and recorded.

quote: The main responsibilities of the independent quality unit(s) should not be delegated.
statement: The main responsibilities of the independent quality unit(s) are not delegated.

quote: These responsibilities should be described in writing
statement: The quality unit responsibilities are written down, and include at least the responsibilities listed in this clause.

quote: Releasing or rejecting all APIs. Releasing or rejecting intermediates for use outside the control of the manufacturing company
statement: The quality unit releases or rejects all APIs, and releases or rejects intermediates that will be used outside the manufacturer's control.

quote: Establishing a system to release or reject raw materials, intermediates, packaging and labelling materials
statement: The quality unit sets up a system for releasing or rejecting raw materials, intermediates, packaging materials and labelling materials.

quote: Reviewing completed batch production and laboratory control records of critical process steps before release of the API for distribution
statement: The quality unit reviews the completed batch production and laboratory control records for critical process steps before an API is released for distribution.

quote: Making sure that critical deviations are investigated and resolved
statement: The quality unit ensures critical deviations are investigated and resolved.

quote: Approving all specifications and master production instructions
statement: The quality unit approves all specifications and master production instructions.

quote: Approving all procedures impacting the quality of intermediates or APIs
statement: The quality unit approves every procedure that affects the quality of intermediates or APIs.

quote: Making sure that internal audits (self-inspections) are performed
statement: The quality unit ensures internal audits (self-inspections) are carried out.

quote: Approving intermediate and API contract manufacturers
statement: The quality unit approves contract manufacturers of intermediates and APIs.

quote: Approving changes that potentially impact intermediate or API quality
statement: The quality unit approves changes that could affect intermediate or API quality.

quote: Reviewing and approving validation protocols and reports
statement: The quality unit reviews and approves validation protocols and validation reports.

quote: Making sure that quality related complaints are investigated and resolved
statement: The quality unit ensures quality-related complaints are investigated and resolved.

quote: Making sure that effective systems are used for maintaining and calibrating critical equipment
statement: The quality unit ensures effective systems are in use for maintenance and calibration of critical equipment.

quote: Making sure that materials are appropriately tested and the results are reported
statement: The quality unit ensures materials are tested appropriately and the results are reported.

quote: Making sure that there is stability data to support retest or expiry dates and storage conditions on APIs and/or intermediates where appropriate
statement: The quality unit ensures, where appropriate, that stability data exist to support the retest or expiry dates and storage conditions of APIs and/or intermediates.

quote: Performing product quality reviews (as defined in Section 2.5)
statement: The quality unit performs product quality reviews as defined in Section 2.5.

quote: A mechanism should be established to demonstrate at a site how the PQS operates across the product lifecycle, in an easily understandable way for management, staff and regulatory inspectors, e.g., a quality manual, documentation, flowcharts, procedures.
statement: A mechanism exists at the site, such as a quality manual, documentation, flowcharts or procedures, that shows management, staff and inspectors in an easily understood way how the PQS works across the product lifecycle.

quote: Companies can implement a program in which the PQS is routinely audited in-house (i.e., internal audit program) to ensure that the system is functioning at a high level.
statement: The company may run an internal audit programme that routinely audits the PQS to confirm it functions at a high level.

quote: The manufacturer is required to comply with the requirements of Good Manufacturing Practices prescribed in Schedule M under the conditions of the licence so as to ensure that the drugs manufacturers in the country conform to the standards prescribed for them.
statement: As a licence condition, the manufacturer complies with the GMP requirements of Schedule M.

quote: If the activity of a distributor or his or her agent is subcontracted to another entity, the person or entity to which the activity is subcontracted shall be appropriately authorized to perform the subcontracted activity and shall uphold the same standards as the distributor.
statement: If a distributor's or agent's activity is subcontracted, the subcontractor is appropriately authorised for that activity and meets the same standards as the distributor.

quote: The activity of distributor and retailer shall be taken under supervision of qualified staff as specified in Drugs Rules 1945.
statement: Distributor and retailer activities are supervised by qualified staff as specified in the Drugs Rules 1945.

quote: This may be reflected in a quality manual.

quote: A designated, competent person shall conduct self-inspection in an independent and detailed way.

quote: There shall be records of self-inspection results which shall contain all observations made during the inspection and if required proposal for corrective measures.

quote: There shall be an effective follow-up programme and evaluation of inspection report and corrective action taken by the management.

quote: Self-inspections should be conducted periodically, according to an annual schedule.
statement: Self-inspections are carried out periodically to an annual schedule.

quote: The team conducting the inspection should be free from bias

quote: individual members should have appropriate knowledge and experience

quote: processes are in place to ensure the management of outsourced activities

quote: may be, in addition, performed on special occasions e.g., in the case of product recall or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the regulatory authorities is announced

quote: The team responsible for self-inspection shall consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of good manufacturing practices objectively.

quote: All recommendations for corrective action shall be implemented.

quote: The procedure for self- inspection shall be documented

quote: there shall be an effective follow- up programme

quote: Management shall appoint a self-inspection team consisting of experts in their respective fields who are familiar with GMP.

quote: The company management shall evaluate both the self-inspection report and the corrective actions as necessary.

quote: It may be useful to supplement self-inspections with a quality audit.

quote: Such audits may also be extended to suppliers and contractors.

quote: The person responsible for quality control shall have responsibility, together with other relevant departments, for approving suppliers who can reliably supply starting and packaging materials that meet established specifications.
statement: The person responsible for quality control, together with other relevant departments, approves suppliers able to reliably supply starting and packaging materials that meet specifications.

quote: Before suppliers are approved and included in the approved suppliers’ list or specifications, they shall be evaluated.

quote: The evaluation shall take into account a supplier’s history and the nature of the materials to be supplied.

quote: The authorised person responsible for approving a batch for release shall always ensure that the following requirements have been met:- (a) the licence and the approval requirements for the product have been met for the batch concerned

quote: the principles and guidelines of GMP, as laid down in this Part, have been followed

quote: the principal manufacturing and testing processes have been validated
statement: Before release, the authorised person confirms that the main manufacturing and testing processes are validated.

quote: all the necessary checks and tests have been performed and account taken of the production conditions and manufacturing records
statement: Before release, the authorised person confirms that all needed checks and tests were done and that production conditions and manufacturing records were taken into account.

quote: any planned changes or deviations in manufacturing or QC have been notified in accordance with a well-defined reporting system before any product is released. Such changes may need notification and approval by the licensing authority

quote: any additional sampling, inspection, tests and checks have been carried out or initiated, as appropriate, to cover planned changes and deviations

quote: all necessary production and QC documentation has been completed and endorsed by supervisors trained in appropriate disciplines
statement: Before release, the authorised person confirms that all needed production and QC documents are complete and signed off by supervisors trained in the relevant disciplines.

quote: appropriate audits, self-inspections and spot-checks are carried out by experienced and trained staff
statement: Before release, the authorised person confirms that appropriate audits, self-inspections and spot-checks are done by experienced, trained staff.

quote: approval has been given by the head of quality control
statement: Before release, the authorised person confirms that the head of quality control has given approval.

quote: all relevant factors have been considered, including the factor associated with the output batch directly under review (e.g., sub-division of output batches from a common input, factors associated with continuous production runs)

quote: Data may be recorded by other means in addition to the computer system.
statement: Where useful, data may also be recorded by means other than the computerised system, alongside it.

quote: The licensee shall prepare a succinct document in the form of ‘Site Master File’ containing specific and factual Good Manufacturing Practices about the production or control or both of pharmaceutical manufacturing preparations carried out at the licensed premises.
statement: The licensee has prepared a concise Site Master File giving specific, factual GMP information on the production and/or control of the pharmaceutical preparations made at the licensed premises.

quote: General information:- (a) brief information of the firm; (b) pharmaceutical manufacturing activities as permitted by the licensing authority; (c) other manufacturing activities, if any, carried out in the premises; (d) type of products licensed for manufacture with flow charts mentioning procedure and process flow; (e) number of employees engaged in the production, quality control, storage and distribution; (f) use of outside scientific, analytical or other technical assistance in relation to manufacture and analysis; (g) products details registered with foreign countries. statement: The Site Master File covers general information: a short profile of the firm, the manufacturing activities permitted by the licensing authority, any other activities on the premises, licensed product types with process flow charts, staff numbers in production, QC, storage and distribution, any outside scientific, analytical or technical help, products registered in foreign countries, and short descriptions of the quality management system, pharmaceutical quality system and quality risk assessment.

quote: Personnel:- (a) organisational chart showing the arrangement for quality assurance including production and quality control; (b) qualifications, experience and responsibilities of key personnel; (c) outline for arrangements for basic and in-service training and how the records are maintained; (d) health requirements for personnel engaged in production; and (e) personnel hygiene requirements, including clothing.

quote: Premises:- (a) simple plan or description of manufacturing areas drawn to scale; (b) nature of construction and fixtures or fittings; (c) brief description of ventilation systems.
statement: The Site Master File covers premises: a scale plan or description of manufacturing areas, the nature of construction and fixtures or fittings, and a short description of the ventilation systems.

quote: More details shall be given for critical areas with potential risk of airborne contamination (schematic drawing of systems).
statement: In the Site Master File, ventilation is described in more detail (with schematic drawings of the systems) for critical areas with a potential risk of airborne contamination.

quote: Classification of the rooms used for the manufacture of sterile products shall be mentioned
statement: The Site Master File states the classification of the rooms used to manufacture sterile products.

statement: The Site Master File also covers special areas for handling highly toxic, hazardous and sensitising materials, a short description of the water system with schematic drawings and its sanitation, and the planned preventive maintenance programme for premises with its recording system.

quote: Equipment:- (a) brief description of major equipment used in production and Quality Control Laboratories (a list of equipment required); (b) description of planned preventive maintenance programmes for equipment and of the recording system; and (c) qualification and calibration including the recording systems and arrangements for computerised systems validation.
statement: The Site Master File covers equipment: a short description and list of major production and QC laboratory equipment, the planned preventive maintenance programme for equipment with its recording system, and qualification and calibration, including recording systems and the arrangements for validating computerised systems.

quote: Sanitation:-availability of written specifications and procedures for cleaning manufacturing areas and equipment.
statement: The Site Master File covers sanitation by showing that written specifications and procedures exist for cleaning manufacturing areas and equipment.

quote: Documentation:- (a) arrangements for the preparation, revision and distribution of; (b) necessary documentation for the manufacture; and (c) any other documentation related to product quality that is not mentioned elsewhere (e.g., microbiological controls about air and water).
statement: The Site Master File covers documentation: how documents are prepared, revised and distributed, the documentation needed for manufacture, and any other product-quality documentation not covered elsewhere (for example microbiological controls of air and water).

quote: Production:- (a) brief description of production operations using, wherever possible, flow sheets and charts specifying important parameters; (b) arrangements for the handling of starting materials, packaging materials, bulk and finished products, including sampling, quarantine, release and storage; (c) arrangements for the handling of rejected materials and products; and (d) brief description of general policy for process validation.
statement: The Site Master File covers production: a short description of production operations, using flow sheets and charts with important parameters wherever possible, how starting materials, packaging materials, bulk and finished products are handled (including sampling, quarantine, release and storage), how rejected materials and products are handled, and the general process validation policy.

quote: Quality Assurance and Control:- (a) documentation system; (b) change control; (c) master validation plan and validation policy; (d) product quality review; and (e) description of the quality control system and of the activities of the QC Department. Procedures for the release of the finished products.
statement: The Site Master File covers quality assurance and control: the documentation system, change control, the master validation plan and validation policy, product quality review, a description of the QC system and QC department activities, and the procedures for releasing finished products.

quote: Manufacture under loan licence and licensee:- description of the way in which compliance of GMP by the loan licensee shall be assessed.
statement: For manufacture under loan licence, the Site Master File describes how the loan licensee's GMP compliance is assessed.

quote: Distribution, complaints and product recall:- (a) arrangements and recording system for distribution; and (b) arrangements for the handling of complaints and product recalls.
statement: The Site Master File covers distribution, complaints and recalls: the arrangements and recording system for distribution, and the arrangements for handling complaints and product recalls.

quote: Self-inspection:- short description of the self-inspection system indicating whether an outside, independent and experienced external expert was involved in evaluating the manufacturer’s compliance with GMP in all aspects of production.
statement: The Site Master File gives a short description of the self-inspection system, stating whether an outside, independent, experienced expert took part in evaluating GMP compliance across all aspects of production.

quote: Export of drugs:- (a) products exported to different countries; and (b) complaints and product recall, if any.
statement: The Site Master File covers export: the products exported to each country and any related complaints and product recalls.

quote: The guidelines published by the World Health Organization (WHO) on following aspects relating to GMP through their Technical Report Series from time to time may be considered for general guidance purposes:- (1) Guidelines on the principles of airflow directions, air filtration standards, temperature, humidity and related parameters. (2) GMP guidelines regarding the design, installation and operation of pharmaceutical water systems including guidance about which quality of water to use for specific applications, such as the manufacture of APIs and dosage forms. (3) Guidelines on design, installation, qualification and maintenance of the HVAC systems of the manufacturing plant. (4) GMP guidelines for validation. (5) Guidelines on packaging of pharmaceutical products.
statement: The site may use WHO Technical Report Series GMP guidelines as general guidance on airflow, air filtration, temperature, humidity and related parameters; design, installation and operation of pharmaceutical water systems and choice of water quality; design, installation, qualification and maintenance of HVAC systems; validation; and packaging.

quote: Technical aspects of the contract shall be drawn up by the competent persons suitably knowledgeable on the specific characteristics of Phytopharmaceuticals, including their production and quality control testing.
statement: The technical parts of any contract are drawn up by competent people with suitable knowledge of phytopharmaceuticals, including their production and quality control testing.

quote: At least one member of the self-inspection team shall possess a thorough knowledge of Phytopharmaceuticals.
statement: At least one member of the self-inspection team has thorough knowledge of phytopharmaceuticals.

quote: A Pharmaceutical Quality System appropriate for the manufacture of medicinal products should ensure that: (i) Product realisation is achieved by designing, planning, implementing, maintaining and continuously improving a system that allows the consistent delivery of products with appropriate quality attributes
statement: The quality system achieves product realisation by designing, planning, implementing, maintaining and continually improving a system that consistently delivers products with the right quality attributes.

quote: Product and process knowledge is managed throughout all lifecycle stages
statement: Product and process knowledge is managed across every lifecycle stage.

quote: Medicinal products are designed and developed in a way that takes account of the requirements of Good Manufacturing Practice
statement: Medicinal products are designed and developed taking GMP requirements into account.

quote: Production and control operations are clearly specified and Good Manufacturing Practice adopted
statement: Production and control operations are clearly defined and GMP is applied.

quote: Managerial responsibilities are clearly specified
statement: Management responsibilities are clearly defined.

quote: Arrangements are made for the manufacture, supply and use of the correct starting and packaging materials, the selection and monitoring of suppliers and for verifying that each delivery is from the approved supply chain
statement: Arrangements exist for making, supplying and using the correct starting and packaging materials, for choosing and monitoring suppliers, and for verifying that each delivery comes from the approved supply chain.

quote: Processes are in place to assure the management of outsourced activities
statement: Processes exist to manage outsourced activities.

quote: A state of control is established and maintained by developing and using effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality
statement: A state of control is set up and kept by building and using effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality.

quote: The results of product and processes monitoring are taken into account in batch release, in the investigation of deviations, and, with a view to taking preventive action to avoid potential deviations occurring in the future
statement: Product and process monitoring results are used in batch release, in deviation investigations, and to take preventive action against future deviations.

quote: All necessary controls on intermediate products, and any other in-process controls and validations are carried out
statement: All necessary controls on intermediate products, other in-process controls and validations are performed.

quote: Continual improvement is facilitated through the implementation of quality improvements appropriate to the current level of process and product knowledge
statement: Continual improvement is supported by putting in place quality improvements suited to current process and product knowledge.

quote: Arrangements are in place for the prospective evaluation of planned changes and their approval prior to implementation taking into account regulatory notification and approval where required
statement: Planned changes are evaluated in advance and approved before implementation, taking account of regulatory notification and approval where required.

quote: After implementation of any change, an evaluation is undertaken to confirm the quality objectives were achieved and that there was no unintended deleterious impact on product quality
statement: After any change is implemented, an evaluation confirms the quality objectives were met and product quality was not harmed unintentionally.

quote: An appropriate level of root cause analysis should be applied during the investigation of deviations, suspected product defects and other problems. This can be determined using Quality Risk Management principles.
statement: A suitable level of root cause analysis is applied when investigating deviations, suspected product defects and other problems; the level can be set using quality risk management principles.

quote: In cases where the true root cause(s) of the issue cannot be determined, consideration should be given to identifying the most likely root cause(s) and to addressing those.
statement: Where the true root cause cannot be found, the most likely root cause(s) are identified and addressed.

quote: Where human error is suspected or identified as the cause, this should be justified having taken care to ensure that process, procedural or system based errors or problems have not been overlooked, if present.
statement: Where human error is suspected or identified as the cause, this is justified after making sure that process, procedural or system errors or problems, if present, were not overlooked.

quote: Appropriate corrective actions and/or preventive actions (CAPAs) should be identified and taken in response to investigations.
statement: Appropriate corrective and/or preventive actions (CAPAs) are identified and taken in response to investigations.

quote: The effectiveness of such actions should be monitored and assessed, in line with Quality Risk Management principles
statement: The effectiveness of CAPAs is monitored and assessed in line with quality risk management principles.

quote: Medicinal products are not sold or supplied before an Authorised Person has certified that each production batch has been produced and controlled in accordance with the requirements of the Marketing Authorisation and any other regulations relevant to the production, control and release of medicinal products
statement: Medicinal products are not sold or supplied until an Authorised Person has certified that each production batch was made and controlled in line with the Marketing Authorisation and other relevant regulations on production, control and release.

quote: Satisfactory arrangements exist to ensure, as far as possible, that the medicinal products are stored, distributed and subsequently handled so that quality is maintained throughout their shelf life
statement: Satisfactory arrangements ensure, as far as possible, that products are stored, distributed and later handled so their quality is kept throughout shelf life.

quote: There is a process for self-inspection and/or quality audit, which regularly appraises the effectiveness and applicability of the Pharmaceutical Quality System
statement: A self-inspection and/or quality audit process regularly appraises how effective and applicable the pharmaceutical quality system is.

quote: The manufacturer and, where different, Marketing Authorisation holder should evaluate the results of the review and an assessment made as to whether corrective and preventive action or any revalidation should be undertaken, under the Pharmaceutical Quality System.
statement: The manufacturer, and the Marketing Authorisation holder where different, evaluate the product quality review results and assess, under the quality system, whether corrective and preventive action or revalidation is needed.

quote: There should be management procedures for the ongoing management and review of these actions and the effectiveness of these procedures verified during self-inspection.
statement: Management procedures exist for the ongoing management and review of the resulting actions, and their effectiveness is verified during self-inspection.

quote: Quality reviews may be PE 009-18 (Part I) -6- 24 September 2026 Chapter 1 Pharmaceutical Quality System grouped by product type, e.g. solid dosage forms, liquid dosage forms, sterile products, etc. where scientifically justified.
statement: Where scientifically justified, quality reviews may be grouped by product type (for example solid, liquid or sterile products).

quote: Where the Marketing Authorisation holder is not the manufacturer, there should be a technical agreement in place between the various parties that defines their respective responsibilities in producing the product quality review.
statement: Where the Marketing Authorisation holder is not the manufacturer, a technical agreement sets out each party's responsibilities for producing the product quality review.

quote: The Authorised Person responsible for final batch certification together with the Marketing Authorisation holder should ensure that the quality review is performed in a timely manner and is accurate.
statement: The Authorised Person responsible for final batch certification and the Marketing Authorisation holder ensure the quality review is done on time and is accurate.

quote: In addition to recalls, there are other potential risk-reducing actions that may be considered in order to manage the risks presented by quality defects. Such actions may include the issuance of cautionary communications to healthcare professionals in relation to their use of a batch that is potentially defective.
statement: Besides recalls, other risk-reducing actions may be considered to manage risks from quality defects, such as sending cautionary communications to healthcare professionals about using a potentially defective batch.

quote: These should be considered on a case-by-case basis and discussed with the concerned Competent Authorities.
statement: Such risk-reducing actions are considered case by case and discussed with the competent authorities concerned.

quote: The main responsibilities of the independent quality unit(s) should not be delegated.
statement: The main responsibilities of the independent quality unit(s) are not delegated.

quote: These responsibilities should be described in writing
statement: The quality unit's responsibilities are set out in writing.

quote: Releasing or rejecting all APIs
statement: The quality unit releases or rejects every API.

quote: Releasing or rejecting intermediates for use outside the control of the manufacturing company
statement: The quality unit releases or rejects intermediates that will be used outside the manufacturer's control.

quote: Establishing a system to release or reject raw materials, intermediates, packaging and labelling materials
statement: The quality unit sets up a system for releasing or rejecting raw materials, intermediates, and packaging and labelling materials.

quote: Reviewing completed batch production and laboratory control records of critical process steps before release of the API for distribution
statement: The quality unit reviews completed batch production and laboratory control records for critical process steps before an API is released for distribution.

quote: Making sure that critical deviations are investigated and resolved
statement: The quality unit makes sure critical deviations are investigated and resolved.

quote: Approving all specifications and master production instructions
statement: The quality unit approves all specifications and master production instructions.

quote: Approving all procedures impacting the quality of intermediates or APIs
statement: The quality unit approves every procedure that affects the quality of intermediates or APIs.

quote: Making sure that internal audits (self-inspections) are performed
statement: The quality unit makes sure internal audits (self-inspections) take place.

quote: Approving intermediate and API contract manufacturers
statement: The quality unit approves contract manufacturers of intermediates and APIs.

quote: Approving changes that potentially impact intermediate or API quality
statement: The quality unit approves changes that could affect intermediate or API quality.

quote: Reviewing and approving validation protocols and reports
statement: The quality unit reviews and approves validation protocols and reports.

quote: Making sure that quality related complaints are investigated and resolved
statement: The quality unit makes sure quality-related complaints are investigated and resolved.

quote: Making sure that effective systems are used for maintaining and calibrating critical equipment
statement: The quality unit makes sure effective systems are used to maintain and calibrate critical equipment.

quote: Making sure that materials are appropriately tested and the results are reported
statement: The quality unit makes sure materials are tested appropriately and results are reported.

quote: Making sure that there is stability data to support retest or expiry dates and storage conditions on APIs and/or intermediates where appropriate
statement: The quality unit makes sure stability data exist to support retest or expiry dates and storage conditions for APIs and/or intermediates, where appropriate.

quote: Performing product quality reviews (as defined in Section 2.6)
statement: The quality unit performs product quality reviews as defined in Section 2.6.

quote: The data governance system should ensure controls over the data lifecycle which are commensurate with the principles of quality risk management.
statement: The data governance system ensures data lifecycle controls proportionate to quality risk management principles.

quote: These controls may be:  Organisational o procedures, e.g. instructions for completion of records and retention of completed records; o training of staff and documented authorisation for data generation and approval; o data governance system design, considering how data is generated, recorded, processed, retained and used, and risks or vulnerabilities are controlled effectively; o routine (e.g. daily, batch- or activity-related) data verification; o periodic surveillance, e.g. self-inspection processes seek to verify the effectiveness of the data governance system; or o the use of personnel with expertise in data management and integrity, including expertise in data security measures.  Technical o computerised system validation, qualification and control; o automation; or o the use of technologies that provide greater controls for data management and integrity.
statement: Data lifecycle controls may include organisational measures (procedures for completing and retaining records, staff training and documented authorisation for generating and approving data, governance system design that controls risks across how data is generated, recorded, processed, retained and used, routine data verification such as daily, batch- or activity-related checks, periodic surveillance such as self-inspection, and staff with data integrity and security expertise) and technical measures (computerised system validation, qualification and control, automation, or technologies giving greater data control).

quote: The effectiveness of data integrity control measures should be assessed periodically as part of self-inspection (internal audit) or other periodic review processes. This should ensure that controls over the data lifecycle are operating as intended.
statement: The effectiveness of data integrity controls is assessed periodically through self-inspection (internal audit) or other periodic reviews, to confirm that data lifecycle controls work as intended.

quote: In addition to routine data verification checks (e.g. daily, batch- or activity- related), self-inspection activities should be extended to a wider review of control measures, including:  A check of continued personnel understanding of good data management practice in the context of protecting of the patient, and ensuring the maintenance of a working environment which is focussed on quality and open reporting of issues (e.g. by review of continued training in good data management principles and expectations).
statement: Beyond routine data verification checks (such as daily, batch- or activity-related checks), self-inspections include a wider review of controls, including a check that staff still understand good data management for patient protection and that the working environment stays quality-focused with open reporting of issues (for example by reviewing ongoing data management training).

quote: A review for consistency of reported data/outcomes against raw entries. This may review data not included during the routine data verification checks (where justified based on risk), and/or a sample of previously verified data to ensure the continued effectiveness of the routine process.
statement: Self-inspections include a review of reported data and outcomes against raw entries, which may cover data not checked routinely (where risk-justified) and/or a sample of already-verified data to confirm the routine process still works.

quote: A risk-based sample of computerised system logs / audit trails to ensure that information of relevance to GMP/GDP activity is reported accurately. This is relevant to situations where routine computerised system data is reviewed manually or by a validated ‘exception report’
statement: Self-inspections include a risk-based sample of computerised system logs and audit trails to confirm GMP/GDP-relevant information is reported accurately, particularly where routine system data is reviewed manually or through a validated exception report.

quote: A review of quality system metrics (i.e. trending) that may also be indicators of data governance effectiveness.
statement: Self-inspections include a review of quality system metrics (trending) that may also indicate how effective data governance is.

quote: The company’s Pharmaceutical Quality System should be able to prevent, detect and correct weaknesses in the system or their processes that may lead to data integrity lapses.
statement: The pharmaceutical quality system can prevent, detect and correct weaknesses in systems or processes that could lead to data integrity lapses.

quote: The company should know their data life cycle and integrate the appropriate controls and procedures such that the data generated will be valid, complete and reliable.
statement: The company knows its data lifecycle and builds in suitable controls and procedures so that generated data are valid, complete and reliable.

quote: Specifically, such control and procedural changes may be in the following areas:  Quality Risk Management,  Investigation programs,  Data review practices (section 9),  Computerised system validation,  IT infrastructure, services and security (physical and virtual),  Vendor/contractor management,  Training program to include company’s approach to data governance and data governance SOPs,  Storage, processing, transfer and retrieval of completed records, including decentralised/cloud-based data storage, processing and transfer activities,  Appropriate oversight of the purchase of GMP/GDP critical equipment and IT infrastructure that incorporate requirements designed to meet data integrity expectations, e.g. User Requirement Specifications, (Refer section 9.2)  Self-inspection program to include data quality and integrity, and  Performance indicators (quality metrics) and reporting to senior management.
statement: Control and procedural changes for data integrity may address areas such as quality risk management, investigations, data review practices, computerised system validation, IT infrastructure, services and security, vendor and contractor management, training on data governance, handling of completed records (including cloud storage), oversight of purchasing critical equipment and IT with data integrity requirements, self-inspection covering data quality and integrity, and quality metrics reported to senior management.

quote: Where summary data is distributed between different sites of the same organisation, the evaluation of the supplying site’s compliance may be determined through alternative means (e.g. evidence of compliance with corporate procedures, internal audit reports, etc.).
statement: Where summary data are shared between sites of the same organisation, the supplying site's compliance may be evaluated by alternative means, such as evidence of following corporate procedures or internal audit reports.

quote: The company’s quality unit should establish a program and schedule to conduct ongoing reviews of audit trails based upon their criticality and the system’s complexity in order to verify the effective implementation of current controls and to detect potential non-compliance issues.
statement: The quality unit sets up a programme and schedule for ongoing audit trail reviews, based on each system's criticality and complexity, to verify current controls work and to detect potential non-compliance.

quote: These reviews should be incorporated into the company’s self-inspection programme.
statement: Audit trail reviews are built into the company's self-inspection programme.

quote: Procedures should be in place to address and investigate any audit trail discrepancies, including escalation processes for the notification of senior management and national authorities where necessary.
statement: Procedures exist to address and investigate audit trail discrepancies, including escalation to senior management and national authorities where necessary.

quote: Audit trail reviews should be both random (selected based on chance) and targeted (selected based on criticality or risk).
statement: Audit trail reviews include both random selections and targeted selections based on criticality or risk.

quote: These elements will vary depending on the source, the supply chain and the subsequent use of the excipient, but as a minimum the following high level GMP elements should be considered by the manufacturing authorisation holder: (a) establishment and implementation of an effective pharmaceutical quality system
statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering, as a minimum and allowing for the excipient's source, supply chain and use, whether an effective pharmaceutical quality system is established and implemented.

quote: sufficient competent and appropriately qualified personnel
statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether there are enough competent, suitably qualified personnel.

quote: defined job descriptions for managerial and supervisory staff responsible for manufacturing and quality activities
statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether managerial and supervisory staff responsible for manufacturing and quality have defined job descriptions.

quote: training programmes for all staff involved in manufacturing and quality activities (included but not limited to cleaning, engineering, laboratory, maintenance, materials management, safety, and technical services)
statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether there are training programmes for all staff in manufacturing and quality activities (including cleaning, engineering, laboratory, maintenance, materials management, safety and technical services).

quote: training programmes related to health, hygiene and clothing as identified as necessary to the intended operations
