statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether there are health, hygiene and clothing training programmes as needed for the intended operations.

quote: provision and maintenance of premises and equipment appropriate to the intended operations
statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether premises and equipment suited to the intended operations are provided and maintained.

quote: documentation system(s) covering all processes and specifications for the various manufacturing and quality operations
statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether documentation systems cover all processes and specifications for manufacturing and quality operations.

quote: systems for coding and identifying starting materials, intermediates and excipients to allow full traceability
statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether systems exist to code and identify starting materials, intermediates and excipients for full traceability.

quote: qualification program of suppliers
statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether there is a supplier qualification programme.

quote: system for quality control of the excipient and a responsible person independent from production to release the batches
statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether there is an excipient quality control system and a responsible person, independent of production, who releases batches.

quote: retention of records for incoming materials and excipients and retention of samples of excipients for the periods required by PIC/S Guide to Good Manufacturing Practice for Medicinal Products, Part II
statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether records for incoming materials and excipients, and samples of excipients, are retained for the periods set by the PIC/S GMP Guide Part II.

quote: systems to ensure that any activity contracted out is subject to a written contract
statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether systems ensure every contracted-out activity is covered by a written contract.

quote: maintenance of an effective system whereby complaints are reviewed and excipients may be recalled
statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether an effective system is maintained for reviewing complaints and recalling excipients.

quote: change management and deviation management system
statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether there is a change management and deviation management system.

quote: environmental control and storage conditions
statement: The manufacturing authorisation holder, in its excipient risk assessment, is considering whether environmental controls and storage conditions are in place.

quote: The distributor should conduct and record self-inspections in order to monitor the implementation of and compliance with these guidelines.
statement: The distributor carries out and records self-inspections to monitor implementation of and compliance with these GDP guidelines.

quote: Regular self-inspections should be performed in accordance with an approved schedule.
statement: Self-inspections are carried out regularly to an approved schedule.

quote: Procedures should be in place for the safe removal of types of waste including toxic waste (chemical and biological), reagents, samples, solvents and air filters.
statement: Procedures exist for safely removing waste, including toxic chemical and biological waste, reagents, samples, solvents and air filters.

quote: The amount of antimicrobial waste being generated by laboratory testing activities is generally considered to be negligible compared to the amounts that are being generated by manufacturing activities but should still be considered in exceptional cases, e.g. if very large amounts of sample are being tested by a quality control laboratory.
statement: Antimicrobial waste from laboratory testing, though usually negligible next to manufacturing waste, is still considered in exceptional cases, such as when a QC laboratory tests very large sample quantities.

quote: manufacturers of APIs and FPPs should consider retaining documentation on the following: ■■ a risk assessment for all contaminants related to antimicrobial manufacturing, in the event that they are released into the environment, and the associated risk of development of resistant microorganisms
statement: API and finished product manufacturers consider keeping a risk assessment of all contaminants from antimicrobial manufacturing if released into the environment, including the risk of resistant microorganisms developing.

quote: based on the above risk assessment, waste-stream analysis for each antimicrobial agent produced (at API sites and FPP sites).
statement: Based on that risk assessment, manufacturers consider keeping a waste-stream analysis for each antimicrobial produced, at API and finished product sites.

quote: This analysis should be repeated whenever there is a change in production affecting waste streams
statement: The waste-stream analysis is repeated whenever a production change affects waste streams.

quote: the quantity and nature of the waste generated, including the analytical data and documentation of analyses performed and their findings on the levels of antimicrobial agents or their precursors
statement: Manufacturers consider keeping records of the quantity and nature of waste generated, including analytical data, documented analyses and findings on levels of antimicrobials or their precursors.

quote: regular reports on the collection, treatment and disposal of waste and wastewater; the frequency should be risk-based and in line with local, regional or international regulatory requirements, as applicable
statement: Manufacturers consider keeping regular reports on collecting, treating and disposing of waste and wastewater, at a risk-based frequency consistent with applicable local, regional or international regulatory requirements.

quote: information on the methods used to treat the waste should be documented to be effective for each specific antimicrobial or antimicrobial precursor.
statement: The waste treatment methods are documented as effective for each specific antimicrobial or antimicrobial precursor.

quote: Analytical data demonstrating the conversion of these substances and their residues to non-hazardous waste materials should be available at the facility and kept up to date
statement: Analytical data showing conversion of these substances and residues to non-hazardous waste are available at the facility and kept current.

quote: if effective waste treatment is not yet implemented for all waste streams resulting from the manufacture of each API or FPP, documentation on a time-limited strategy should be in place, with specified milestones for that implementation, specifying actions towards achieving treatment that significantly reduces the concentration of the antimicrobial substance or its precursor (and its microbial source, when relevant)
statement: If effective treatment is not yet in place for all waste streams from each API or finished product, a documented time-limited strategy with specified milestones sets out actions towards treatment that significantly reduces the antimicrobial or precursor concentration (and its microbial source, when relevant).

quote: a rationale and risk assessment as to why the manufacturer selected specific methods of decontamination of manufacturing waste containing antimicrobials and/or their mitigation strategy
statement: Manufacturers consider keeping a rationale and risk assessment for their chosen decontamination methods for antimicrobial-containing manufacturing waste and/or their mitigation strategy.

quote: Incineration may also be considered for solid or semi-liquid waste.
statement: Incineration may be considered for solid or semi-liquid waste.

quote: The zero-liquid effluent approach or zero-discharge policy is encouraged, especially when the risk is assessed to be high or unclear, as it prevents any contamination of the environment.
statement: A zero-liquid effluent or zero-discharge approach is adopted, especially where the risk is assessed as high or unclear.

quote: The level of effectiveness and by-products should be considered when adopting a particular approach.
statement: The effectiveness and by-products of a treatment approach are considered when choosing it.

quote: It is recommended that this documentation be maintained at the manufacturing facility regardless of whether or not an external contractor has been used.
statement: This waste documentation is kept at the manufacturing facility even when an external contractor is used.

quote: These points to consider should be used by manufacturers as part of their self-audits, in order to verify their continued level of GMP compliance.
statement: Manufacturers use these points to consider in their self-audits to verify continued GMP compliance.

quote: The quality system should ensure that: ■■ GSP and GDP are adopted and implemented to ensure that the quality of medical products is maintained throughout their shelf- life in the supply chain
statement: GSP and GDP are adopted and implemented so product quality is maintained throughout shelf life in the supply chain.

quote: medical products are appropriately procured, stored, distributed and delivered (in compliance with the legislation) to the appropriate recipients (see Section 18.1)
statement: Medical products are procured, stored, distributed and delivered appropriately, in compliance with legislation, to appropriate recipients.

quote: operations are clearly specified in written procedures
statement: Operations are clearly set out in written procedures.

quote: responsibilities are clearly specified in job descriptions
statement: Responsibilities are clearly set out in job descriptions.

quote: all risks are identified and necessary, effective controls are implemented
statement: All risks are identified and necessary, effective controls are put in place.

quote: processes are in place to assure the management of outsourced activities
statement: Processes exist to manage outsourced activities.

quote: there is a procedure for self-inspection and quality audits
statement: A procedure exists for self-inspection and quality audits.

quote: there is a system for quality risk management
statement: A quality risk management system exists.

quote: there are systems for managing returns, complaints and recalls
statement: Systems exist for managing returns, complaints and recalls.

quote: there are systems to manage changes, deviations and corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs)
statement: Systems exist for managing changes, deviations and CAPAs.

quote: The quality system should include self-inspections.
statement: The quality system includes self-inspections.

quote: These should be conducted to monitor the implementation, compliance with and effectiveness of SOPs, as well as compliance with regulations, GSP, GDP and other appropriate guidelines.
statement: Self-inspections monitor implementation of, compliance with and effectiveness of SOPs, and compliance with regulations, GSP, GDP and other relevant guidelines.

quote: Self-inspections should be conducted periodically, according to an annual schedule.
statement: Self-inspections are carried out periodically according to an annual schedule.

quote: The team conducting the inspection should be free from bias
statement: The self-inspection team is free from bias.

quote: individual members should have appropriate knowledge and experience.
statement: Each self-inspection team member has appropriate knowledge and experience.

quote: The results of all self-inspections should be recorded.
statement: Results of every self-inspection are recorded.

quote: Reports should contain all observations made during the inspection and presented to the relevant personnel and management.
statement: Self-inspection reports include all observations and are presented to relevant personnel and management.

quote: Necessary CAPAs should be taken
statement: Necessary CAPAs are taken.

quote: their effectiveness should be reviewed within a defined timeframe.
statement: CAPA effectiveness is reviewed within a defined timeframe.

quote: Users should conduct audits and self-inspection of water systems at regular intervals.
statement: Users audit and self-inspect their water systems at regular intervals.

quote: Records should be maintained.
statement: Records of water system audits and self-inspections are kept.

quote: Data governance control strategies using quality risk management (QRM) principles (5) are required to prevent or mitigate risks.
statement: Data governance control strategies based on quality risk management principles are in place to prevent or mitigate risks.

quote: The control strategy should aim to implement appropriate technical, organizational and procedural controls.
statement: The control strategy aims to put in place appropriate technical, organisational and procedural controls.

quote: Examples of controls may include, but are not limited to: ■■ the establishment and implementation of procedures that will facilitate compliance with data integrity requirements and expectations; ■■ the adoption of a quality culture within the company that encourages personnel to be transparent about failures, which includes a reporting mechanism inclusive of investigation and follow-up processes; ■■ the implementation of appropriate controls to eliminate or reduce risks to an acceptable level throughout the life cycle of the data; ■■ ensuring sufficient time and resources are available to implement and complete a data integrity programme; to monitor compliance with data integrity policies, procedures and processes through e.g. audits and self-inspections; and to facilitate continuous improvement of both; ■■ the assignment of qualified and trained personnel and provision of regular training for personnel in, for example, GxP, and the principles of data integrity in computerized systems and manual/ paper based systems; ■■ the implementation and validation of computerized systems appropriate for their intended use, including all relevant data integrity requirements in order to ensure that the computerized system has the necessary controls to protect the electronic data (3); and ■■ the definition and management of the appropriate roles and responsibilities for contract givers and contract acceptors, entered into quality agreements and contracts including a focus on data integrity requirements.
statement: Controls may include procedures supporting data integrity compliance, a quality culture that encourages transparent reporting of failures with investigation and follow-up, controls that remove or reduce data risks to an acceptable level across the data life cycle, enough time and resources for a data integrity programme, monitoring through audits and self-inspections and continuous improvement, qualified and trained staff with regular GxP and data integrity training, validated computerised systems with the controls needed to protect electronic data, and defined roles and responsibilities for contract givers and acceptors in quality agreements and contracts with a focus on data integrity.

quote: There should be a system for the regular review of data for consistency with ALCOA+ principles. This includes paper records and electronic records in day-to-day work, system and facility audits and self-inspections.
statement: A system exists for regularly reviewing data for consistency with ALCOA+ principles, covering paper and electronic records in daily work and in system and facility audits and self-inspections.

quote: The effectiveness of the controls implemented should be evaluated through, for example: ■■ the tracking and trending of data; ■■ a review of data, metadata and audit trails (e.g. in warehouse and material management, production, quality control, case report forms and data processing); and ■■ routine audits and/or self-inspections, including data integrity and computerized systems.
statement: The effectiveness of implemented controls is evaluated, for example by tracking and trending data, reviewing data, metadata and audit trails (in areas such as warehouse and materials management, production, QC, case report forms and data processing), and routine audits and/or self-inspections that cover data integrity and computerised systems.

quote: The quality manager should ensure the establishment, implementation and maintenance of standard operating procedures for all administrative and technical operations
statement: The quality manager ensures SOPs are established, implemented and maintained for all administrative and technical laboratory operations.

quote: personnel matters, including qualiﬁcations and training
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for personnel matters, including qualifications and training.

quote: control of documents, records and data integrity
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for control of documents, records and data integrity.

quote: corrective and preventive actions
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for corrective and preventive actions.

quote: purchase and receipt of consignments of supplies (for example, reagents and materials)
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for purchase and receipt of supplies such as reagents and materials.

quote: procurement, preparation and control of reference substances and reference materials
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for procurement, preparation and control of reference substances and materials.

quote: qualiﬁcation of equipment, including calibration
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for equipment qualification, including calibration.

quote: preventive maintenance and veriﬁcation of instruments and equipment
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for preventive maintenance and verification of instruments and equipment.

quote: internal labelling and storage of materials and solutions
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for internal labelling and storage of materials and solutions.

quote: sampling, if performed by the laboratory
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for sampling, where the laboratory performs it.

quote: testing of samples with descriptions of the methods and equipment used
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for sample testing, describing the methods and equipment used.

quote: validation and verification of analytical procedures
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for validation and verification of analytical procedures.

quote: validity of test results
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for validity of test results.

quote: atypical and out-of-specification results
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for atypical and out-of-specification results.

quote: risks and opportunities
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for risks and opportunities.

quote: cleaning of laboratory facilities, including bench tops, equipment, workstations, clean rooms (aseptic suites) and glassware
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for cleaning of laboratory facilities, including bench tops, equipment, workstations, aseptic clean rooms and glassware.

quote: monitoring of environmental conditions (for example, temperature and humidity)
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for monitoring of environmental conditions such as temperature and humidity.

quote: monitoring of storage conditions
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for monitoring of storage conditions.

quote: disposal of reagents, standards and samples
statement: The quality manager ensures an SOP is in place for disposal of reagents, standards and samples.

quote: Any situation that may lead to a potential deviation or nonconformity should be adequately addressed, leading to preventive action.
statement: Any situation that could lead to a potential deviation or nonconformity is adequately addressed through preventive action.

quote: Preventive actions can be treated as a risk or as an opportunity, depending on the type of potential impact of the action (see subsection 4.4).
statement: Preventive actions can be handled as a risk or as an opportunity, depending on the kind of potential impact (see subsection 4.4).

quote: A standard operating procedure should be established, incorporating a detailed procedure for the planning and performance of the audits, which will: ■■ ensure that internal audits are planned and scheduled periodically by the quality manager (at least once a year) to enable systematic assessments
statement: An SOP sets out detailed planning and performance of audits, with internal audits planned and scheduled periodically by the quality manager, at least once a year, for systematic assessment.

quote: define the scope of each audit and use risk-based criteria to determine the most critical activities to be audited, including the implementation of corrective and preventive actions after the last audit, if relevant
statement: Under the audit SOP, each audit's scope is defined and risk-based criteria pick the most critical activities to audit, including follow-up of CAPAs from the last audit where relevant.

quote: ensure that audits are carried out by trained personnel who are independent of the activity to be audited
statement: Under the audit SOP, audits are done by trained staff independent of the activity audited.

quote: ensure that the results of the audits (audit conclusion) are reported to relevant management, discussed during management review (see subsection 3.10), and communicated to staff
statement: Under the audit SOP, audit conclusions are reported to relevant management, discussed at management review (see subsection 3.10) and shared with staff.

quote: implement appropriate corrections and corrective actions without delay should any nonconformity be identified
statement: Under the audit SOP, appropriate corrections and corrective actions are implemented without delay if any nonconformity is found.

quote: monitor the effectiveness of the implemented corrective actions
statement: Under the audit SOP, the effectiveness of implemented corrective actions is monitored.

quote: retain records as evidence of the implementation of the audit programme and the audit results
statement: Under the audit SOP, records are kept as evidence of the audit programme's implementation and of audit results.

quote: The laboratory should have the following managerial and technical personnel: ■■ A laboratory director (or manager or head of the laboratory, or an appropriate job title) with appropriate qualiﬁcations (university degree in an appropriate discipline) for the position, with experience in a supervisory role in pharmaceutical analysis in a quality control laboratory, in the regulatory sector or in industry, who assumes full responsibility for all operations, including analytical, organizational, administrative and educational.
statement: The laboratory has a director (or equivalent head) with a relevant university degree and supervisory experience in pharmaceutical analysis in a QC laboratory, regulatory body or industry, who holds full responsibility for all analytical, organisational, administrative and educational operations.

quote: This person is also responsible for ensuring that: –– members of the laboratory staff have the competencies and qualifications appropriate to their required functions and their grades reﬂect their responsibilities
statement: The laboratory director ensures staff have competencies and qualifications suited to their functions and that their grades match their responsibilities.

quote: the adequacy of existing training procedures for staff is reviewed periodically
statement: The laboratory director ensures that the adequacy of existing staff training procedures is reviewed periodically.

quote: the technical management is adequately supervised
statement: The laboratory director ensures that technical management is adequately supervised.

quote: the certiﬁcates of analysis, analytical test reports and other important reports and protocols are approved
statement: The laboratory director ensures that certificates of analysis, analytical test reports and other important reports and protocols are approved.

quote: The laboratory director should preferably be supported and complemented by one or more technical managers (or senior analysts) with extensive experience in pharmaceutical analysis in a quality control laboratory, who have been designated responsibility for the analytical operations and for direct management and supervision of the team of analysts and technicians.
statement: The laboratory director is supported, preferably, by one or more technical managers or senior analysts with extensive QC pharmaceutical analysis experience who are designated responsible for analytical operations and for directly managing and supervising analysts and technicians.

quote: A quality manager who shall have the responsibility and authority to implement and ensure compliance with the QMS and quality control activities.
statement: The laboratory has a quality manager with the responsibility and authority to implement the QMS and quality control activities and ensure compliance with them.

quote: The quality manager should remain independent of routine laboratory analytical activities, depending on the size of the laboratory.
statement: Depending on laboratory size, the quality manager stays independent of routine analytical work.

quote: The quality manager organizes internal audits of various laboratory activities, with the participation, preferably, of another member of staff from another section, according to a schedule approved during the management review.
statement: The quality manager organises internal audits of laboratory activities, preferably with a staff member from another section, to a schedule approved at management review.

quote: The quality manager, with the support of technical managers whenever necessary, ensures that: –– personnel operating speciﬁc equipment, instruments or other devices are competent for the tasks they are performing
statement: The quality manager, supported by technical managers as needed, ensures that staff operating specific equipment, instruments or devices are competent for those tasks.

quote: personnel involved in tests or calibrations, validations or veriﬁcations are competent for the tasks they are performing
statement: The quality manager ensures that staff doing tests, calibrations, validations or verifications are competent for those tasks.

quote: regular in-service training programmes are arranged to update and extend the skills of both analysts and technicians
statement: The quality manager ensures regular in-service training is arranged to update and extend the skills of analysts and technicians.

quote: the laboratory participates regularly in suitable proﬁciency testing schemes and, whenever possible, collaborative studies (as applicable)
statement: The quality manager ensures the laboratory takes part regularly in suitable proficiency testing schemes and, where possible and applicable, collaborative studies.

quote: due arrangements are made for the safekeeping and control of substances that are subject to poison regulation or to the controls applied to narcotic, psychotropic and radioactive substances, and which should be stored under lock and key, and handled and used in designated places under the supervision of an authorized person
statement: The quality manager ensures due arrangements for safekeeping and control of poisons and narcotic, psychotropic and radioactive substances, which are kept locked up and handled and used only in designated places under an authorised person's supervision.

quote: Qualified analysts, who normally should be graduates in pharmacy, analytical chemistry or other relevant subject, with the requisite knowledge, skills and ability to adequately perform the tasks assigned to them by managers or supervisors.
statement: The laboratory has qualified analysts, normally graduates in pharmacy, analytical chemistry or another relevant subject, with the knowledge, skills and ability to perform their assigned tasks.

quote: Appropriately qualified and experienced analysts with a thorough understanding of the management system, including the review, interpretation and reporting of test results, the maintenance of an internal chain of custody, and proper implementation of corrective and preventive actions in response to analytical problems, should also be available to serve as laboratory supervisors.
statement: Suitably qualified, experienced analysts with a thorough grasp of the management system (including reviewing, interpreting and reporting results, the internal chain of custody, and CAPAs for analytical problems) are available to act as laboratory supervisors.

quote: Technicians should hold diplomas in their subjects awarded by technical or vocational schools or have the requisite hands-on experience to perform the assigned activities.
statement: Technicians hold diplomas in their subjects from technical or vocational schools, or have the hands-on experience needed for their assigned activities.

quote: The laboratory should have an appropriate training schedule for staff, particularly for those staff who respond to the technical and managerial needs of the laboratory.
statement: The laboratory has an appropriate staff training schedule, especially for staff who meet its technical and managerial needs.

quote: Inputs to the training plan can be gathered from internal audits, management reviews, risk and opportunity assessments, or other available options.
statement: Inputs to the training plan may be drawn from internal audits, management reviews, risk and opportunity assessments or other available sources.

quote: On successful completion of training, the results of evaluation should be recorded and made available, and the information should be added to the competency matrix or master list.
statement: After training is completed successfully, evaluation results are recorded and made available, and the competency matrix or master list is updated.

quote: The quality management system should ensure that: ■ sufficient resources are available (for example, equipment, personnel, materials)
statement: The QMS ensures sufficient resources, such as equipment, personnel and materials.

quote: excipients for pharmaceutical use are produced, controlled, stored and distributed in accordance with the recommendations in this document and other associated guidelines, such as good quality control laboratory practices and good storage and distribution practices, where appropriate
statement: Excipients for pharmaceutical use are produced, controlled, stored and distributed in line with this guidance and associated guidelines, such as good QC laboratory practices and good storage and distribution practices, where appropriate.

quote: managerial roles, responsibilities and authorities are clearly specified in job descriptions
statement: Managerial roles, responsibilities and authorities are clearly set out in job descriptions.

quote: operations and other activities are clearly described in a written form, such as standard operating procedures and work instructions
statement: Operations and other activities are clearly described in writing, for example SOPs and work instructions.

quote: appropriate arrangements are made for the manufacture, supply and use of the correct containers and labels
statement: Appropriate arrangements exist for making, supplying and using the correct containers and labels.

quote: all necessary controls are in place
statement: All necessary controls are in place.

quote: calibrations, verification or validations are carried out where necessary
statement: Calibrations, verifications or validations are done where necessary.

quote: the excipient for pharmaceutical use is correctly processed and checked according to the defined procedures and specifications
statement: The excipient is processed and checked correctly against defined procedures and specifications.

quote: deviations, suspected product defects, out-of-specification test results and any other nonconformances or incidents are reported, investigated and recorded
statement: Deviations, suspected product defects, OOS results and other nonconformances or incidents are reported, investigated and recorded.

quote: An appropriate level of root cause analysis is applied during such investigations and the most likely root causes are identified
statement: A suitable level of root cause analysis is applied in these investigations and the most likely root causes are identified.

quote: proposed changes are evaluated and approved prior to implementation
statement: Proposed changes are evaluated and approved before implementation.

quote: After implementation of a change that could impact the quality or the product, an evaluation should be undertaken to confirm that the quality objectives were achieved and that there was no unintended adverse impact on product quality
statement: After a change that could affect quality or the product is implemented, an evaluation confirms the quality objectives were met and there was no unintended adverse effect on product quality.

quote: appropriate corrective actions and preventive actions, as well as checks on the effectiveness of those actions (where appropriate), are identified and taken
statement: Appropriate corrective and preventive actions, and checks of their effectiveness where appropriate, are identified and taken.

quote: where required, processes are in place to ensure the management of any outsourced activities that may impact product quality, purity and integrity
statement: Where required, processes exist to manage outsourced activities that could affect product quality, purity and integrity.

quote: a batch of an excipient for pharmaceutical use is not released and supplied before it has been released by the quality unit with the assurance that the batch has been produced and controlled in accordance with product specifications, and with the recommendations in this document and any other regulations relevant to the production, control and release of these products
statement: No excipient batch is released and supplied until the quality unit has released it, assured that it was produced and controlled in line with product specifications, this guidance and other relevant regulations on production, control and release.

quote: there is a system for handling complaints, returns and recalls
statement: A system exists for handling complaints, returns and recalls.

quote: there is a system for self-inspection
statement: A self-inspection system exists.

quote: there is a system for product quality review
statement: A product quality review system exists.

quote: Management should ensure that the quality management system achieves its intended objectives and measures managing and performance in areas such as: ■ self-inspections, inspections, quality audits and supplier’s audits ■ complaints, returns and recalls ■ changes and deviations ■ rejected batches ■ quality control, out-of-specification results and out-of-trend results ■ maintenance ■ qualification and validation ■ corrective and preventive actions ■ risk management.
statement: Management ensures the quality management system meets its intended objectives and measures how it is managed and how it performs in areas such as self-inspections, inspections, quality and supplier audits; complaints, returns and recalls; changes and deviations; rejected batches; quality control, OOS and OOT results; maintenance; qualification and validation; CAPA; and risk management.

quote: There should be written standard operating procedures and programmes for periodic self-inspections, quality audits and supplier audits.
statement: Written SOPs and programmes exist for periodic self-inspections, quality audits and supplier audits.

quote: Self-inspections should be performed routinely in accordance with a self- inspection programme.
statement: Self-inspections are carried out routinely, following a self-inspection programme.

quote: The team responsible for self-inspection should consist of personnel with the appropriate knowledge and experience.
statement: The self-inspection team is made up of staff with suitable knowledge and experience.

quote: Team members may be from inside or outside the manufacturer
statement: Self-inspection team members can be drawn from inside or outside the manufacturer.

quote: members of the team should be free from bias.
statement: Self-inspection team members are free from bias.

quote: Areas to be covered in self-inspections may include: ■ premises ■ personnel ■ equipment ■ maintenance and calibration ■ storage conditions of materials and finished products ■ production and in-process controls ■ quality control ■ documentation, data generation and data integrity ■ change control and deviations management ■ complaints and recalls ■ qualification and validation ■ cleaning procedures.
statement: Self-inspections can cover areas such as premises, personnel, equipment, maintenance and calibration, storage conditions of materials and finished products, production and in-process controls, quality control, documentation and data integrity, change control and deviations, complaints and recalls, qualification and validation, and cleaning procedures.

quote: The excipient’s end use should be considered during inspection of excipient manufacturers. It is particularly important to know whether the excipient will be used in the preparation of a sterile dosage form.
statement: When inspecting an excipient manufacturer, the intended end use of the excipient is taken into account, in particular whether it will be used to prepare a sterile dosage form.

quote: The excipient manufacturer is responsible for ensuring that excipients are pyrogen free if the manufacturer makes such a representation in specifications, labels or a drug master file.
statement: Where the excipient manufacturer claims in specifications, labels or a drug master file that an excipient is pyrogen free, the manufacturer ensures that it is.

quote: Standard operating procedures and associated records should be available for at least the following: ■ equipment ■ analytical apparatus and instruments ■ out-of-specification results ■ maintenance and calibration ■ cleaning and sanitization ■ personnel matters, such as training, clothing and hygiene ■ qualification and validation ■ self-inspection and audits ■ complaints ■ recalls ■ returns.
statement: SOPs and related records are available covering at minimum: equipment; analytical apparatus and instruments; OOS results; maintenance and calibration; cleaning and sanitization; personnel matters such as training, clothing and hygiene; qualification and validation; self-inspection and audits; complaints; recalls; and returns.

quote: Manufacturers should implement measures to continuously improve the quality management system, manufacturing and testing procedures, and the quality of their products.
statement: The manufacturer puts in place measures for continual improvement of the quality management system, of manufacturing and testing procedures, and of product quality.

quote: These measures may include the review of root causes of nonconformances, quality complaint investigations and outcomes, and results from self-inspections, audits and other trends.
statement: Improvement measures can include reviewing root causes of nonconformances, complaint investigations and their outcomes, and results of self-inspections, audits and other trends.

quote: The self-inspection programme should be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of GMP and to rec- ommend the necessary corrective actions.
statement: The self-inspection programme is designed to find any gaps in how GMP is implemented and to recommend the corrective actions needed.

quote: Self-inspections should be performed routinely
statement: Self-inspections are carried out routinely.

quote: may be, in addition, performed on special occasions, e.g. in the case of product recalls or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the health authorities is announced
statement: Additional self-inspections can be carried out on special occasions, for example after product recalls or repeated rejections, or when a health authority inspection is announced.

quote: The team responsible for self-inspection should consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of GMP objectively
statement: The self-inspection team is made up of people able to assess GMP implementation objectively.

quote: all recommenda- tions for corrective action should be implemented
statement: All recommended corrective actions from self-inspection are implemented.

quote: The procedure for self-inspection should be documented
statement: The self-inspection procedure is documented.

quote: there should be an effec- tive follow-up programme
statement: An effective follow-up programme for self-inspections is in place.

quote: Written instructions for self-inspection should be established to provide a minimum and uniform standard of requirements.
statement: Written self-inspection instructions are established that set a minimum, uniform standard of requirements.

quote: These may include questionnaires on GMP requirements covering at least the following items: (a) personnel (b) premises including personnel facilities (c) maintenance of buildings and equipment (d) storage of starting materials and finished products (e) equipment (f) production and in-process controls (g) quality control (h) documentation (i) sanitation and hygiene (j) validation and revalidation programmes (k) calibration of instruments or measurements systems (l) recall procedures (m) complaints management (n) labels control (o) results of previous self-inspections and any corrective steps taken.
statement: Self-inspection instructions can include GMP questionnaires covering at least: personnel; premises including personnel facilities; maintenance of buildings and equipment; storage of starting materials and finished products; equipment; production and in-process controls; quality control; documentation; sanitation and hygiene; validation and revalidation programmes; calibration of instruments or measurement systems; recall procedures; complaints management; labels control; and results of earlier self-inspections and corrective steps taken.

quote: Management should appoint a self-inspection team from local staff who are expert in their own fields and familiar with GMP.
statement: Management appoints a self-inspection team of local staff who are experts in their own fields and familiar with GMP.

quote: The members of the team may be appointed from inside or outside the company.
statement: Self-inspection team members can be appointed from inside or outside the company.

quote: The frequency at which self-inspections are conducted may de- pend on company requirements.
statement: The site can set how often self-inspections are done according to company requirements.

quote: A report should be made at the completion of a self-inspection.
statement: A report is prepared when each self-inspection is completed.

quote: The report should include: (a) self-inspection results (b) evaluation and conclusions (c) recommended corrective actions.
statement: The self-inspection report contains the results, the evaluation and conclusions, and the recommended corrective actions.

quote: The company management should evaluate both the self- inspection report and the corrective actions as necessary.
statement: Company management evaluates the self-inspection report and the corrective actions, as necessary.

quote: It may be useful to supplement self-inspections with a quality audit.
statement: The site can supplement self-inspections with a quality audit.

quote: Such audits may also be extended to suppliers and contractors.
statement: Quality audits can be extended to suppliers and contractors.

quote: The main responsibilities of the independent quality unit(s) should not be delegated.
statement: The main responsibilities of the independent quality unit(s) are not delegated.

quote: These responsibilities should be described in writing
statement: The quality unit's responsibilities are described in writing.

quote: Releasing or rejecting all APIs.
statement: The quality unit releases or rejects every API.

quote: Releasing or rejecting intermediates for use outside the control of the manufacturing company.
statement: The quality unit releases or rejects intermediates that will be used outside the manufacturing company's control.

quote: Establishing a system to release or reject raw materials, intermediates, packaging and labelling materials.
statement: The quality unit sets up a system for releasing or rejecting raw materials, intermediates, and packaging and labelling materials.

quote: Reviewing completed batch production and laboratory control records of critical process steps before release of the API for distribution.
statement: The quality unit reviews completed batch production and laboratory control records for critical process steps before the API is released for distribution.

quote: Making sure that critical deviations are investigated and resolved.
statement: The quality unit makes sure critical deviations are investigated and resolved.

quote: Approving all speciﬁcations and master production instructions.
statement: The quality unit approves all specifications and master production instructions.

quote: Approving all procedures impacting the quality of intermediates or APIs.
statement: The quality unit approves every procedure that affects the quality of intermediates or APIs.

quote: Making sure that internal audits (self-inspections) are performed.
statement: The quality unit makes sure internal audits (self-inspections) are carried out.

quote: Approving intermediate and API contract manufacturers.
statement: The quality unit approves contract manufacturers of intermediates and APIs.

quote: Approving changes that potentially impact quality of intermediates or APIs.
statement: The quality unit approves changes that could affect the quality of intermediates or APIs.

quote: Reviewing and approving validation protocols and reports.
statement: The quality unit reviews and approves validation protocols and reports.

quote: Making sure that quality-related complaints are investigated and resolved.
statement: The quality unit makes sure quality-related complaints are investigated and resolved.

quote: Making sure that effective systems are used for maintaining and calibrating critical equipment.
statement: The quality unit makes sure effective systems are used to maintain and calibrate critical equipment.

quote: Making sure that materials are appropriately tested and the results are reported.
statement: The quality unit makes sure materials are properly tested and results are reported.

quote: Making sure that there are stability data to support retest or expiry dates and storage conditions on APIs and/or intermediates where appropriate.
statement: Where appropriate, the quality unit makes sure stability data exist to support retest or expiry dates and storage conditions for APIs and/or intermediates.

quote: Performing product quality reviews (as deﬁned in section 2.5).
statement: The quality unit performs product quality reviews as defined in section 2.5.

quote: Audit ﬁndings and corrective actions should be documented and brought to the attention of the responsible management of the ﬁrm.
statement: Audit findings and corrective actions are documented and reported to the firm's responsible management.

quote: Agreed corrective actions should be completed in a timely and effective manner.
statement: Agreed corrective actions are completed in a timely and effective way.

quote: product realization is achieved by designing, qualifying, planning, implementing, maintaining and continuously improving a system that allows the consistent delivery of products with appropriate quality attributes
statement: The PQS ensures product realization through a system that is designed, qualified, planned, implemented, maintained and continually improved so products with appropriate quality attributes are delivered consistently.

quote: product and process knowledge is managed throughout all life- cycle stages
statement: The PQS ensures product and process knowledge is managed across all life-cycle stages.

quote: pharmaceutical products are designed and developed in a way that takes account of the requirements of GMP and other associated codes such as those of good laboratory practice (GLP) and good clinical practice (GCP)
statement: The PQS ensures products are designed and developed taking account of GMP and related codes such as GLP and GCP.

quote: production and control operations are clearly specified in a written form and GMP requirements are adopted
statement: The PQS ensures production and control operations are clearly specified in writing and GMP requirements are adopted.

quote: managerial responsibilities are clearly specified in job descriptions
statement: The PQS ensures managerial responsibilities are clearly set out in job descriptions.

quote: arrangements are made for the manufacture, supply and use of the correct starting and packaging materials, the selection and monitoring of suppliers and for verifying that each delivery is the correct material from the approved supply chain
statement: The PQS ensures arrangements exist for making, supplying and using the correct starting and packaging materials, for selecting and monitoring suppliers, and for verifying that each delivery is the correct material from the approved supply chain.

quote: all necessary controls on starting materials, intermediate products, and bulk products and other in-process controls, calibrations and validations are carried out
statement: The PQS ensures all necessary controls on starting materials, intermediates and bulk products, plus other in-process controls, calibrations and validations, are carried out.

quote: the finished product is correctly processed and checked, according to the defined procedures
statement: The PQS ensures the finished product is correctly processed and checked following defined procedures.

quote: pharmaceutical products are not sold or supplied before the authorized persons (see also sections 9.11 and 9.12) have certified that each production batch has been produced and controlled in accordance with the requirements of the marketing authorization and any other regulations relevant to the production, control and release of pharmaceutical products
statement: The PQS ensures no product is sold or supplied until the authorized persons (see sections 9.11 and 9.12) have certified that each batch was produced and controlled in line with the marketing authorization and any other regulations on production, control and release.

quote: processes are in place to assure the management of outsourced activities
statement: The PQS ensures processes exist to manage outsourced activities.

quote: satisfactory arrangements exist to ensure, as far as possible, that the pharmaceutical products are stored, distributed and subsequently handled so that quality is maintained throughout their shelf-life
statement: The PQS ensures adequate arrangements exist so that, as far as possible, products are stored, distributed and handled in a way that keeps their quality throughout shelf-life.

quote: there is a procedure for self-inspection and/or quality audit that regularly appraises the effectiveness and applicability of the PQS
statement: The PQS ensures a self-inspection and/or quality audit procedure exists that regularly assesses how effective and applicable the PQS is.

quote: product and processes are monitored and the results taken into account in batch release, in the investigation of deviations and, with a view to taking preventive action to avoid potential deviations occurring in the future
statement: The PQS ensures products and processes are monitored and the results are used in batch release, in deviation investigations, and to take preventive action against future deviations.

quote: arrangements are in place for the prospective evaluation and approval of planned changes and their approval prior to implementation taking into account regulatory notification and approval where required
statement: The PQS ensures planned changes are evaluated and approved in advance, before implementation, taking regulatory notification and approval into account where required.

quote: After implementation of any change, an evaluation is undertaken to confirm that the quality objectives were achieved and that there was no unintended adverse impact on product quality
statement: The PQS ensures that after any change is implemented, an evaluation confirms the quality objectives were met and product quality was not unintentionally harmed.

quote: regular reviews of the quality of pharmaceutical products are conducted with the objective of verifying the consistency of the process and identifying where there is a need for improvement
statement: The PQS ensures regular product quality reviews are carried out to verify process consistency and identify where improvement is needed.

quote: a state of control is established and maintained by developing and using effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality
statement: The PQS ensures a state of control is established and kept through effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality.

quote: continual improvement is facilitated through the implementation of quality improvements appropriate to the current level of process and product knowledge
statement: The PQS ensures continual improvement is supported by implementing quality improvements suited to current process and product knowledge.

quote: there is a system for QRM
statement: The PQS ensures a quality risk management system exists.

quote: deviations, suspected product defects and other problems are reported, investigated and recorded
statement: The PQS ensures deviations, suspected product defects and other problems are reported, investigated and recorded.

quote: An appropriate level of root cause analysis is applied during such investigations.
statement: A suitable level of root cause analysis is applied when investigating deviations, suspected defects and other problems.

quote: The most likely root cause(s) should be identified and appropriate corrective actions and/or preventive actions (CAPAs) should be identified and taken.
statement: Investigations identify the most likely root cause(s), and suitable corrective and/or preventive actions (CAPAs) are identified and carried out.

quote: The effectiveness of CAPAs should be monitored.
statement: The effectiveness of CAPAs is monitored.

quote: Regular, periodic or rolling quality reviews of all pharmaceutical products, including export-only products, should be conducted with the objective of verifying the consistency of the existing process and the appropriateness of current specifications for both starting materials and finished product, to highlight any trends and to identify product and process improvements.
statement: Regular, periodic or rolling quality reviews are carried out for every product, export-only products included, to verify process consistency and that current starting material and finished product specifications are still appropriate, to show trends and to identify product and process improvements.

quote: Such reviews should normally be conducted and documented annually, taking into account previous reviews
statement: Product quality reviews are normally performed and documented annually, taking earlier reviews into account.

quote: review of starting materials and packaging materials used for the product, especially those from new sources and in particular the review of supply chain traceability of active substances
statement: The quality review covers starting and packaging materials used, especially those from new sources, and in particular the supply chain traceability of active substances.

quote: a review of critical in-process controls, and finished product results
statement: The quality review covers critical in-process controls and finished product results.

quote: a review of all batches that failed to meet established specification(s) and their investigation
statement: The quality review covers every batch that failed its specification(s) and the related investigation.

quote: a review of all significant deviations or non-conformances, the related investigations and the effectiveness of resultant CAPAs taken
statement: The quality review covers all significant deviations or non-conformances, their investigations, and how effective the resulting CAPAs were.

quote: a review of all changes made to the processes or analytical methods
statement: The quality review covers all changes to processes or analytical methods.

quote: a review of dossier variations submitted, granted or refused
statement: The quality review covers dossier variations submitted, granted or refused.

quote: a review of the results of the stability monitoring programme and any adverse trends
statement: The quality review covers stability monitoring programme results and any adverse trends.

quote: a review of all quality-related returns, complaints and recalls and the investigations performed at the time
statement: The quality review covers all quality-related returns, complaints and recalls and the investigations done at the time.

quote: a review of adequacy of any other previous corrective actions on product processes or equipment
statement: The quality review covers whether any other earlier corrective actions on product processes or equipment were adequate.

quote: post-marketing commitments for new dossiers and variations to the dossiers
statement: The quality review covers post-marketing commitments for new dossiers and dossier variations.

quote: the qualification status of relevant equipment and utilities, e.g. heating, ventilation and air-conditioning (HVAC), water or compressed gases and a review of the results of monitoring the output of such equipment and utilities
statement: The quality review covers the qualification status of relevant equipment and utilities (for example HVAC, water or compressed gases) and the results of monitoring their output.

quote: a review of technical agreements to ensure that they are up to date
statement: The quality review covers technical agreements to confirm they are current.

quote: The manufacturer and, where different, marketing authorization holder, should evaluate the results of the review and an assessment should be made as to whether CAPA or any revalidation should be undertaken, under the PQS.
statement: The manufacturer, and the marketing authorization holder where different, evaluate the review results and assess, within the PQS, whether CAPA or revalidation is needed.

quote: CAPAs should be completed in a timely and effective manner, according to documented procedures.
statement: CAPAs arising from the review are completed promptly and effectively following documented procedures.

quote: There should be procedures for the ongoing management and review of these actions
statement: Procedures exist for the ongoing management and review of these CAPAs.

quote: the effectiveness of these procedures should be verified during self-inspection
statement: Self-inspection verifies that the CAPA management and review procedures are effective.

quote: Quality reviews may be grouped by product type, e.g. solid dosage forms, liquid dosage forms, or sterile products, where scientifically justified.
statement: Where scientifically justified, quality reviews can be grouped by product type, for example solid, liquid or sterile dosage forms.

quote: Where the marketing authorization holder is not the manufacturer, there should be a technical agreement in place between the various parties that defines their respective responsibilities in producing the quality review.
statement: If the marketing authorization holder is not the manufacturer, a technical agreement between the parties sets out each party's responsibilities for producing the quality review.

quote: The authorized person responsible for final batch certification, together with the marketing authorization holder, should ensure that the quality review is performed in a timely manner and is accurate.
statement: The authorized person responsible for final batch certification, jointly with the marketing authorization holder, ensures the quality review is done on time and is accurate.

quote: The self- inspection programme should be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of GMP and to recommend the necessary corrective actions.
statement: The self-inspection programme is designed to find any gaps in how GMP is implemented and to recommend the corrective actions needed.

quote: Self-inspections should be performed routinely
statement: Self-inspections are carried out routinely.

quote: may be, in addition, performed on special occasions, e.g. in the case of product recalls or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the health authorities is announced
statement: Additional self-inspections can be carried out on special occasions, for example after product recalls or repeated rejections, or when a health authority inspection is announced.

quote: The team responsible for self-inspection should consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of GMP objectively.
statement: The self-inspection team is made up of people able to assess GMP implementation objectively.

quote: All recommendations for corrective action should be implemented.
statement: All recommended corrective actions from self-inspection are implemented.

quote: The procedure for self-inspection should be documented
statement: The self-inspection procedure is documented.

quote: there should be an effective follow-up programme
statement: An effective follow-up programme for self-inspections is in place.

quote: Written instructions for self-inspection should be established to provide a minimum and uniform standard of requirements.
statement: Written self-inspection instructions are established that set a minimum, uniform standard of requirements.

quote: These may include questionnaires on GMP requirements covering at least the following items: (a) personnel; (b) premises including personnel facilities; (c) maintenance of buildings and equipment; (d) storage of starting materials and finished products; (e) equipment; (f) production and in-process controls; (g) QC; (h) documentation; (i) sanitation and hygiene; (j) validation and revalidation programmes; (k) calibration of instruments or measurement systems; (l) recall procedures; (m) complaints management; (n) labels control; (o) results of previous self-inspections and any corrective steps taken.
statement: Self-inspection instructions can include GMP questionnaires covering at least: personnel; premises including personnel facilities; maintenance of buildings and equipment; storage of starting materials and finished products; equipment; production and in-process controls; QC; documentation; sanitation and hygiene; validation and revalidation programmes; calibration of instruments or measurement systems; recall procedures; complaints management; labels control; and results of earlier self-inspections and corrective steps taken.

quote: Management should appoint a self-inspection team consisting of experts in their respective fields who are familiar with GMP.
statement: Management appoints a self-inspection team of experts in their own fields who are familiar with GMP.

quote: The members of the team may be appointed from inside or outside the company.
statement: Self-inspection team members can be appointed from inside or outside the company.

quote: The frequency with which self-inspections are conducted may depend on company requirements but should preferably be at least once a year.
statement: Self-inspection frequency can follow company requirements but is preferably at least once a year.

quote: The frequency should be stated in the procedure.
statement: The self-inspection procedure states the self-inspection frequency.

quote: A report should be made at the completion of a self-inspection.
statement: A report is prepared when each self-inspection is completed.

quote: The report should include: (a) self-inspection results; (b) evaluation and conclusions; (c) recommended corrective actions.
statement: The self-inspection report contains the results, the evaluation and conclusions, and the recommended corrective actions.

quote: There should be an effective follow-up programme.
statement: An effective follow-up programme for self-inspections is in place.

quote: The company management should evaluate both the self-inspection report and the corrective actions as necessary.
statement: Company management evaluates the self-inspection report and the corrective actions, as necessary.

quote: It may be useful to supplement self-inspections with a quality audit.
statement: The site can supplement self-inspections with a quality audit.

quote: Such audits may also be extended to suppliers and contractors (see section 7, “Contract production and analysis”).
statement: Quality audits can be extended to suppliers and contractors.

quote: The person responsible for QC should have responsibility, together with other relevant departments, for approving suppliers who can reliably supply starting and packaging materials that meet established specifications.
statement: The person responsible for QC, with other relevant departments, is responsible for approving suppliers that can reliably supply starting and packaging materials meeting established specifications.

quote: Before suppliers are approved and included in the approved suppliers’ list or specifications, they should be evaluated.
statement: Suppliers are evaluated before being approved and added to the approved suppliers' list or specifications.

quote: The evaluation should take into account a supplier’s history and the nature of the materials to be supplied.
statement: Supplier evaluation considers the supplier's history and the nature of the materials to be supplied.

quote: If an audit is required, it should determine the supplier’s ability to conform with GMP standards.
statement: Where a supplier audit is required, it determines whether the supplier can comply with GMP standards.

quote: the marketing authorization and the manufacturing authorization requirements for the product have been met for the batch concerned
statement: Before releasing a batch, the authorized person ensures the marketing and manufacturing authorization requirements for the product were met for that batch.

quote: the principles and guidelines of GMP, as laid down in the guidelines published by WHO, have been followed
statement: Before releasing a batch, the authorized person ensures WHO GMP principles and guidelines were followed.

quote: the principal manufacturing and testing processes have been validated
statement: Before releasing a batch, the authorized person ensures the principal manufacturing and testing processes are validated.

quote: all the necessary checks and tests have been performed and account taken of the production conditions and manufacturing records
statement: Before releasing a batch, the authorized person ensures all necessary checks and tests were done and production conditions and manufacturing records were taken into account.

quote: any planned changes or deviations in manufacturing or QC have been notified in accordance with a well-defined reporting system before any product is released. Such changes may need notification to, and approval by, the medicines regulatory authority
statement: Before releasing a batch, the authorized person ensures any planned changes or deviations in manufacturing or QC were notified through a well-defined reporting system before release, including notification to and approval by the medicines regulatory authority where needed.

quote: any additional sampling, inspection, tests and checks have been carried out or initiated, as appropriate, to cover planned changes and deviations
statement: Before releasing a batch, the authorized person ensures any additional sampling, inspection, tests and checks needed to cover planned changes and deviations were carried out or started, as appropriate.

quote: all necessary production and QC documentation has been completed and endorsed by supervisors trained in appropriate disciplines
statement: Before releasing a batch, the authorized person ensures all required production and QC documentation is complete and endorsed by supervisors trained in the relevant disciplines.

quote: appropriate audits, self-inspections and spot-checks are carried out by experienced and trained staff
statement: Before releasing a batch, the authorized person ensures suitable audits, self-inspections and spot-checks are carried out by experienced, trained staff.

quote: approval has been given by the head of QC
statement: Before releasing a batch, the authorized person ensures the head of QC has given approval.

quote: all relevant factors have been considered, including any not specifically associated with the output batch directly under review (e.g. subdivision of output batches from a common input, factors associated with continuous production runs)
statement: Before releasing a batch, the authorized person ensures all relevant factors were considered, including those not directly tied to the batch under review (for example subdivision of output batches from a common input, or continuous production run factors).
